candidates.computation_change_reason: The header ties effluent concentration (Ce) to derived instream waste concentrations (e.g., 2.13*Ce, Cd,dom, Cd, Cd,hh) and separates those from ambient criteria columns; different readings of whether Ce is a measured value, modeled input, or enforceable limit would change which numeric limit applies and how exceedances are calculated.

This row supplies a non-blank effluent concentration (10 ug/l) alongside computed instream values and multiple criteria endpoints (domestic 1, acute aquatic 19, chronic aquatic 15, human health 30); interpreting which field is the operative discharge limit versus a modeled intermediate value would change limit applicability and exceedance determinations.

The row reports Ce=2.11 with derived instream concentrations and a domestic criterion of 10500 ug/l; whether Ce is treated as an enforceable effluent limit, a projection, or a reported measurement affects which numeric standard governs compliance comparison.

Unlike most pollutants in the table, livestock/irrigation and wildlife criteria are marked N/A rather than 1E+100 while aquatic and human-health criteria are numeric; different interpretations of N/A (criterion inapplicable vs. missing data vs. non-limiting) could change which criterion is treated as binding for limit selection.

Ambient and effluent concentration cells are blank while downstream instream columns read 0; treating blanks as zero/no-discharge versus absent monitoring evidence would change whether a numeric limit comparison is applicable (A) and whether missing effluent data reflects a documented no-data state or unresolved monitoring (C).

The row omits an MQL value and leaves ambient/effluent cells blank while listing acute (28) and chronic (6.6) aquatic criteria; whether this indicates the pollutant is not monitored, monitored without quantitation, or subject to criteria-only evaluation would change monitoring-obligation findings (B), missing-evidence classification (C), and whether numeric limits can be applied (A).

The MQL column appears for most listed pollutants but is absent for some rows; interpreting MQL as establishing required analytical sensitivity versus descriptive method metadata would change which monitoring obligations are deemed applicable (B) and how sub-quantitation or missing results are classified (C).

The trailing N/A appears in the Need TMDL column for every pollutant row in this segment; interpreting N/A as confirming no TMDL-based limit applies versus leaving TMDL limit applicability unresolved would change whether TMDL-derived numeric limits enter discharge-limit computation.

The domestic criterion (0.048 ug/l) is orders of magnitude below the human-health criterion (0.18 ug/l) with instream concentrations shown as 0; interpretation of significant figures, rounding, or whether zero instream values foreclose comparison affects which criterion controls and whether an exceedance can be evaluated.
